command:
set -e; codex exec --help | head -120; cat > /tmp/lcl-dashboard-prompt.txt <<'EOF'
Work ONLY in this repository and on the current branch. Read AGENTS.md first and obey its UX/design rules. This task is the first UI polish pass for the Local Climate Link mobile Dashboard. Do not change Shelly/BLE/automation-core semantics, safety behavior, networking, persistence formats, or unrelated architecture. Reuse existing runtime/control APIs and components; do not invent parallel logic. Keep changes small, clean, typed, testable, and avoid god components.

Accepted visual direction from the user: compact calm native smart-home dashboard. Top title on one row; refresh and settings as equal compact icon actions aligned on the right; no filler subtitle or redundant kicker; compact climate/time segmented selector; dense readable automation cards; temperature as primary reading, humidity secondary; ON/OFF and Auto/Manual controls visible without making the card tall; minimal borders/shadows; no decorative filler; preserve useful information unless explicitly removed.

User-requested fixes that MUST be addressed now:
1. Remove the dashboard description equivalent to 'Podgląd tego, co aktualnie widzi i robi każde Shelly.' with no replacement copy. Remove redundant Dashboard kicker if it only adds height.
2. Fix settings/refresh asymmetry and the global settings action pushing page content downward. Make the top actions compact, equal and aligned with the Dashboard heading using the smallest coherent shell/header change.
3. Make climate automation cards substantially shorter while retaining useful current information and project touch-target rules.
4. Restore visible ON/OFF and Manual/Auto controls on climate cards using the exact existing runtime-control semantics already used elsewhere. Do not create new automation behavior. Correctly represent pending/disabled/error states.
5. When the last automation is removed, route directly to the existing 'Co chcesz zrobić?' intent screen instead of showing a redundant empty Dashboard. Zero-installation startup and post-delete must converge to that screen.
6. Keep time automation cards visually coherent and do not break schedule behavior.
7. Use design tokens/shared primitives; no hardcoded theme colors.

Before editing inspect AutomationDashboardScreen, TimeAutomationCard, App/App shell, AppRoutes, InstallationDetail/TimeInstallationDetail and existing runtime control hooks/components. Implement the smallest coherent change. Add/update focused tests for zero-state routing and Dashboard controls where practical. Do not commit or push; leave the working tree changed for outer verification.
EOF
codex exec -C . "$(cat /tmp/lcl-dashboard-prompt.txt)"
